facts.text: Wann, Nebraska sprang to life in 1902 when the Sioux City and Western Railroad negotiated with landowner Andrew Allen Wilson, who donated ten acres for the townsite.
Wilson chose the modest name Wann from a list of suggestions, honoring his family and agreeing that no liquor would ever be sold in town.
A post office operated in Wann from 1908 until its closure in 1950, serving the community for forty‑two years.
The Pleasant Valley Church of Christ, built debt‑free in the 1880s, expanded in 1928 and again during 1942‑43 to host worship, education, and community events.
Wann experiences a humid continental climate with hot, humid summers and cold, snowy winters, a growing season that stretches from May through September.
The landscape is dominated by corn and soybean fields, interspersed with prairie remnants and small woodlots of cottonwood, willow, and oak that line nearby streams.
